an0137.user: I'm losing my mind over attribution. We sell scheduling+billing SaaS to clinics, mostly push via email + Meta retargeting, ₹11.5L spend last 30 days. Meta's dashboard says ROAS 3.9. But my Shopify last-click report says 1.7 on the same period. Post-iOS everything's a mess. One of these dashboards is lying to me — how do I figure out which one is the real number?
an0137.assistant:
Neither one is lying, and that's the part you have to accept: both are biased in opposite directions, and the truth sits somewhere between 1.7 and 3.9. Meta's 3.9 is modelled — it counts 7-day-click and view-through conversions it can't fully see post-iOS, so it over-credits itself. Shopify last-click gives the entire sale to whatever the customer touched last (usually a branded search or direct visit), so it under-credits the Meta ad that actually planted the intent. You're refereeing two scoreboards that will never agree, and refreshing them hoping one converges is wasted energy.

Stop trying to pick a winner. Anchor on a number neither dashboard can spin: blended CAC. Take your total spend across everything — ₹11.5L — and divide by the actual count of NEW customers Shopify recorded that month. That single figure is what you're really paying to acquire someone, and it doesn't care which channel claims the assist. Manage to that, set a target you can defend against your contribution per clinic, and let the platform ROAS numbers be directional mood-lighting, not truth.

Caveat: blended CAC blurs channel-level efficiency, so once it's stable, run the occasional geo-holdout or a spend-down test on Meta to see what actually moves — that's the only clean way to size incrementality when the dashboards won't cooperate.

an0138.assistant:
Don't touch anything. A 17% CAC move on 95 conversions isn't a trend — it's noise. At that volume the week-to-week confidence band is easily ±20-25%, so a 17% swing is fully inside what randomness produces even when nothing about your account changed. The real risk here isn't the CAC bump; it's you. Overhauling strategy off one noisy week is how founders whipsaw their accounts into the ground — you reset learning, you lose the comparison baseline, and next week's reversion gets misread as 'the fix worked.'

What would actually count as a signal: the same direction holding for 3-4 weeks straight, or a single move big enough to clear the noise — think CAC up 40%+ and staying there. Until then, let it run and judge it on a trailing 4-week average, not a 7-day snapshot.
